name: Turnaround Tuesday
note: The primary variable is a calendar position, not a price feature. The first trading session of each calendar week -- Monday, or whatever day actually opens the week when Monday is a holiday, detected from the bar timestamps rather than from a holiday table -- is bought at its close if it closed below its own open (req_open) and below the previous session's close (req_prev). The position is sold at the close of the first later session that closes above the session before it, or unconditionally after max_days sessions. On intraday bars the session close is read at entry_min (15:55 ET) because a rule that used the final print would be deciding on a bar it cannot yet have seen; the previous session's close is a completed fact and is used as one. DEVIATION: the optional trend filter is a mean of the last sma_n SESSION closes, not SMA(200) -- 200 sessions cannot form inside the 120-day windows this study runs, so the filter is swept short (sma_gate: 0 off, 1 dip-only below the mean, -1 above it). Known ceiling: one entry per calendar week means at most ~17 trades per symbol in a 120-day window, below the 20-trade minimum the search requires before it will score a symbol. The family fires correctly and is here for its near-zero correlation with everything else in the book, but it will need a longer window than the standard round to be scored at all.
source: Oddmund Groette / Quantified Strategies, 'The Turnaround Tuesday trading strategy' -- listed on their public S&P 500 strategies index (verified via the mirrored index text at github.com/taashareef11112/Po3). CAVEAT carried from the idea: the article body and its equity curve are behind a Cloudflare bot wall, so the construction is confirmed but the reported returns are not. Tested from scratch.

def _et(bars):
    """Minute-of-day, session index, weekday and day-of-month, in New York.

    Bars carry UTC timestamps; every calendar rule here is a New York rule, so
    the offset has to be resolved per bar rather than assumed."""
    import datetime
    mins = []
    sess = []
    dow = []
    dom = []
    last = None
    s = -1
    for b in bars:
        ts = str(b["t"])
        y = int(ts[0:4]); mo = int(ts[5:7]); d = int(ts[8:10])
        hh = int(ts[11:13]); mi = int(ts[14:16])
        if mo < 3 or mo > 11:
            dst = False
        elif 3 < mo < 11:
            dst = True
        elif mo == 3:
            w = datetime.date(y, 3, 1).weekday()
            dst = d >= 1 + ((6 - w) % 7) + 7
        else:
            w = datetime.date(y, 11, 1).weekday()
            dst = d < 1 + ((6 - w) % 7)
        t = (datetime.datetime(y, mo, d, hh, mi)
             - datetime.timedelta(minutes=240 if dst else 300))
        key = (t.year, t.month, t.day)
        if key != last:
            last = key
            s += 1
        mins.append(t.hour * 60 + t.minute)
        sess.append(s)
        dow.append(t.weekday())
        dom.append(t.day)
    return mins, sess, dow, dom


def family_init(ctx):
    bars = ctx.bars
    n = len(bars)
    mins, sess, dow, dom = _et(bars)
    if len(set(str(b["t"])[:10] for b in bars)) == n:
        mins = [955] * n

    emin = int(ctx.p.entry_min)
    req_o = int(ctx.p.req_open)
    req_p = int(ctx.p.req_prev)
    gate = int(ctx.p.sma_gate)
    sn = max(2, int(ctx.p.sma_n))

    # ---- session frame, regular hours only ----
    order = []
    sopen = {}
    sclose = {}
    swd = {}
    for j in range(n):
        if not (570 <= mins[j] < 960):
            continue
        s = sess[j]
        if s not in sopen:
            sopen[s] = float(bars[j]["o"])
            swd[s] = dow[j]
            order.append(s)
        sclose[s] = float(bars[j]["c"])
    pos = dict((s, k) for k, s in enumerate(order))

    # the eval bar of each session: the first bar at or after entry_min
    ev = [False] * n
    seen = set()
    for j in range(n):
        s = sess[j]
        if s in pos and mins[j] >= emin and s not in seen:
            seen.add(s)
            ev[j] = True

    # the first session of each calendar week
    weekfirst = set()
    for k, s in enumerate(order):
        if k == 0:
            continue
        if swd[s] <= swd[order[k - 1]]:
            weekfirst.add(s)

    sig = [0] * n
    for j in range(n):
        if not ev[j]:
            continue
        s = sess[j]
        k = pos[s]
        if s not in weekfirst or k < 1:
            continue
        px = float(bars[j]["c"])          # the close as it stands at 15:55
        if req_o and not (px < sopen[s]):
            continue
        if req_p and not (px < sclose[order[k - 1]]):
            continue
        if gate:
            if k < sn:
                continue
            w = [sclose[order[k - q]] for q in range(1, sn + 1)]
            mu = sum(w) / len(w)
            if gate > 0 and not (px < mu):
                continue
            if gate < 0 and not (px > mu):
                continue
        sig[j] = 1

    # per-bar view of the session frame, for the exit
    sidx = [-1] * n
    pclose = [None] * n
    for j in range(n):
        s = sess[j]
        if s in pos:
            sidx[j] = pos[s]
            k = pos[s]
            if k >= 1:
                pclose[j] = sclose[order[k - 1]]

    ctx.sig = ctx.series(sig, "tt_entry")
    ctx.ev = ctx.series(ev, "tt_eval")
    ctx.sk = ctx.series(sidx, "tt_session")
    ctx.pc = ctx.series(pclose, "tt_prev_close")


def signal(ctx, i):
    return int(ctx.sig[i])


def exit_signal(ctx, i):
    """Out on the first session that closes up on the one before it, and out
    unconditionally after max_days sessions."""
    if not ctx.positions:
        return False
    e = min(p["entry_i"] for p in ctx.positions)
    k = ctx.sk[i]
    ke = ctx.sk[e]
    if k < 0 or ke < 0:
        return False
    if k - ke >= int(ctx.p.max_days):
        return True
    if k <= ke or not ctx.ev[i]:
        return False
    pc = ctx.pc[i]
    return pc is not None and ctx.c[i] > pc
